data.note:
Correct call: **DNA replication** for methotrexate. Verified: PubChem CID 126941, IUPAC (2S)-2-[[4-[(2,4-diaminopteridin-6-yl)methyl-methylamino]benzoyl]amino]pentanedioic acid, structure agrees with BBBC021 (e21). ChEMBL CHEMBL34259 mechanism: Dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor (CHEMBL202) (e21). BBBC021 annotation as DNA replication correct: methotrexate is antimetabolite antifolate, inhibits DHFR -> depletes THF, purine/pyrimidine pools, blocks DNA synthesis.

Phenotype matched: 4 wells 0.01-3 µM (e7,e2,e8,e3):
- nuc_dna_mean z -9.8 to -12.7, nuc_dna_integrated dose-response Spearman rho -1.0 p=0 (e13) value 285 vs DMSO 374 at 0.01 µM down to 274 at 3 µM
- cell_area z +8.9 to +5.6, cell_major_axis +7.1 to +5.2, nuc_major_axis +7.0 to +3.8, cell_nuc_area_ratio up
- cell_count z -2 to -3.8, frac_mitotic_like 0 vs 0.015 DMSO (e14), consistent with S-phase arrest, loss of mitotics
- retained tubulin/actin networks (e5 microscopist: no microtubule depolymerization/bundling, no actin collapse, no monopolar/multipolar spindles), ruling out microtubule, actin, Aurora, Eg5.

Atlas: NSC vote 2/4 DNA replication (e9) vs 1 kinase, 1 microtubule destabilizer; per-well best matches: floxuridine (DNA replication) 0.831 at 0.01 µM and 0.669 at 0.1 µM; top k-neighbors DNA replication 4/10. Strongest similarity aligns with antimetabolite class.

Literature (search_literature): Antimetabolites review [PMID 22049385] and Methotrexate and Pralatrexate [PMID 26433846] describe DHFR inhibition mechanism. Molecular basis of antifolate resistance [PMID 17333344] and Methotrexate resistance review [PMID 40088855] detail nucleotide depletion. Drug-induced megaloblastic change [PMID 6450011] explains enlarged cells/nuclei with impaired DNA content seen here as compensatory growth without division.

Next step proposed (EdU + PI flow + pCHK1/pRPA) remains appropriate to confirm reduced DNA synthesis vs DNA damage checkpoint.

reflection.text:
Unblinded as methotrexate, CID 126941, ChEMBL DHFR inhibitor (CHEMBL202) - scored correct as DNA replication (agent 0.61). This fits the antimetabolite/antifolate class PMID 22049385, PMID 26433846, PMID 17333344 where DHFR inhibition depletes nucleotide pools and blocks DNA synthesis.

What got right: The 4 acquired wells spanning 0.01 to 3 uM (e7, e2, e8, e3) were internally consistent and carried the call. All showed extreme low nuc_dna_mean z -9.8 to -12.7 and low nuc_dna_integrated with rho=-1.0 p=0 (e13), together with enlarged cell_area z +5.6 to +8.9 and increased nuc major axis / cell_nuc_area_ratio (e2, e7, e8). That pattern - reduced DNA content per nucleus despite larger cells - is classically described as megaloblastic change for drug-induced folate antagonism PMID 6450011 and matches DNA replication stress rather than mitotic arrest. Reduced density vs DMSO (e5) with low frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.77 (e14) and retained tubulin/actin (e17 rho=-0.80 p=0.2, e18 rho=-0.40 p=0.6) argued against microtubule destabilizer or strong kinase cytoskeletal effects, supporting e15 hypothesis DNA replication 0.60.

What misled / was weak: Early atlas comparison on 2 wells (e4) voted Kinase inhibitors 1/2 with k-neighbour tie 4/10 kinase vs 4/10 DNA replication, and even with 4 wells (e9) NSC was only 2/4 DNA replication with same 4/10 tie. That tie reflects phenotypic overlap in size and low DNA intensity between replication inhibitors and some kinase inhibitors at screen resolution. Dose-response power was low: n=4 doses gave non-significant p for cell_area (e10 p=0.2), nuc_area (e11 p=0.4), cell_count (e12 p=1.0), nuc_eccentricity (e16 p=0.6) and frac_mitotic (e14 p=0.23). Only integrated DNA was monotonic. The microscopist (e5) - 8 observations, density lower, candidates unknown - added no MoA discrimination.

Why acquisition choices mattered: Sampling low-mid-high doses early (e2 at 0.1 uM, e3 at 3 uM then e7 0.01 uM and e8 1 uM) prevented a single-well call and allowed the rho calculations that showed the integrated DNA dose trend despite non-significant area trends. Without e7 at the lowest active dose, the large cell phenotype could have been dismissed as toxicity. Without e8 at 1 uM we would have lacked the mid-range replication of the low-DNA signal.

No clinical inference is made; this is an in vitro MCF-7 screening phenotype consistent with the known in vitro mechanism of methotrexate as an antimetabolite DHFR inhibitor leading to DNA replication inhibition.
